pathway.title: Teleflex Inc — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage is moderate because debt was repaid, not because earnings grew, and the ratio depends on the earnings base. After the OEM sale closed Teleflex repaid USD 700.0 million of Term A-2 and USD 490.0 million of the revolver, yet the 2.82x reported net leverage becomes 4.01x on FY2025 EBITDA and 3.21x without USD 50.3 million of settlement and tariff-refund gains. On the reported basis the pro forma readings are 2.92x after USD 41.4 million of repurchases made after 2026-09-30 and 1.56x if the sale for about USD 530 million closes; the OEM tax effect is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C11; calculation C12

Earnings improved, but more than a tenth of last-twelve-months EBITDA is one-off. The EBITDA margin is 18.67% against 14.86% in FY2025, yet the USD 25.0 million patent settlement gain and USD 25.3 million of tariff refunds are 11.95% of EBITDA, and without them the margin is 16.44% and nine-month gross margin is 58.27% instead of the reported 59.8%. Further tariff refunds may arrive in the fourth quarter but no receivable is recorded, and quality remediation and excess inventory charges already weigh on gross margin. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 42–44; calculation C11

The retained core earns well, but Interventional is the swing factor for earnings. Vascular and Surgical earned segment margins of 38.12% and 45.10% and grew nine-month revenue 7.2% and 8.4% without acquisitions, while Interventional earned 10.37%, saw third-quarter revenue fall 2.6%, and has a goodwill cushion of about 15% that a 1% rise in the discount rate would cut below 5%. Its profit is 13.21% of segment profit but 32.77% of nine-month operating income after unallocated costs, so losing all of it would cut operating income by about a third, although segment profit would still be 4.11% above the nine-month 2025 total. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 48–50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42; calculation C03

Cash conversion is solid, but shareholder payments outran it. Last-twelve-months free cash flow was USD 242.99 million, 57.71% of EBITDA, on capital spending of only 3.47% of net revenues, yet dividends and repurchases took 2.53 times that amount. Nine-month operating cash flow also benefited from lower tax payments, vendor payment timing and receipts from the settlement and refunds, which may not repeat. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 53; calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C07

Liquidity and maturities are comfortable, and the open questions are cost and covenant headroom. Only USD 87.5 million of borrowings fall due within 12 months, cash alone equals 86.09% of the USD 500.0 million of notes due 2028-06-01, the undrawn revolver is up to USD 940 million before letters of credit, and the revolver and Term A-1 now mature on 2031-05-26. EBITDA covers the run-rate coupon cost of the debt outstanding 5.04x, or 4.43x without the one-offs, and floating-rate debt is 38.72% of principal against 62.26% at 2025-12-31; the replaced 2027 notes cost 1.25 percentage points less than the new 2032 notes. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 91; calculation C08; calculation C09; calculation C10

Financial policy is the main unknown. No leverage target or agency rating is stated, the chief executive and the Chair changed in 2026, three directors joined and two left, and an activist wants strategic alternatives reviewed. Since 2026-07-01 Teleflex repaid 3.40 times as much bank debt as it spent on stock, but USD 400.0 million of the repurchase authorisation remains and the programme may be suspended at any time, so the commitment to debt is a record, not a rule. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 60

The business profile is adequate rather than strong. Nine-month net revenues were USD 1,686.4 million, and continuing operations are 60.44% of FY2025 combined revenue; about three quarters of nine-month growth was acquired, no customer concentration or market share is disclosed, and 42.91% of nine-month revenue comes from outside North America, where most customer relationships outside the United States are with government entities. Against that, substantially all revenue is single-use devices used in high-acuity procedures, and existing-product volumes rose USD 37.7 million. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation C01

runs.text: The five strongest credit supports, in order of weight, follow.

Low capital intensity and positive free cash flow carry debt service from operations. Capital spending is 3.47% of net revenues and last-twelve-months free cash flow was USD 242.99 million, 57.71% of EBITDA, so interest and scheduled repayments are met without refinancing; the caveat is that conversion has swung between 0.49% and 79.73% over recent years. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C05; calculation C06

Vascular and Surgical earn high margins and grow without acquisitions. Segment margins of 38.12% and 45.10% on revenue growth of 7.2% and 8.4% in nine months give operating leverage on volume and price, which lets the core carry the debt while Interventional is repaired. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 48–50; calculation C03

Debt was cut and maturities were extended. Principal fell by USD 1,018.125 million to USD 1,631.875 million, the revolver and Term A-1 now run to 2031-05-26, and the first note maturity is USD 500.0 million on 2028-06-01, so no refinancing event is due in the next 12 months beyond USD 87.5 million of current borrowings. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; calculation C14

Interest cost is covered with room. EBITDA covers the run-rate coupon cost of the debt outstanding 5.04x, or 4.43x without the one-offs, and floating-rate debt fell to 38.72% of principal, which limits rate sensitivity to USD 6.32 million a year for each percentage point. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C08; calculation C09

Demand is for consumable devices used in high-acuity procedures, and existing-product volumes grew in 2026. A USD 37.7 million rise in nine-month volumes supports base cash flow visibility, although it is only 2.65% of the prior-year base. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation C01
The five most material credit weaknesses, in order of weight, follow.

Financial policy is unstated and shareholder payments exceed free cash flow. Dividends and repurchases took 2.53 times last-twelve-months free cash flow, USD 400.0 million of authorisation remains, no leverage target is stated and the board and management changed in 2026, so leverage is a result of the first proceeds and not a commitment. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C07

Interventional margin, volume and goodwill cushion are weak. The segment earned 10.37% against 14.10%, revenue fell 2.6% in the third quarter, the goodwill cushion is about 15% and a 1% rise in the discount rate would cut it below 5%, and its profit is 32.77% of nine-month operating income, so a shortfall would reach earnings and book equity at once. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42; calculation C03

Earnings carry one-offs and temporary support. USD 50.3 million of settlement and tariff-refund gains are 11.95% of EBITDA, and nine-month operating cash flow benefited from lower tax payments and vendor payment timing, so underlying leverage is higher than the reported ratio. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 53; calculation C11

The fourth-quarter OEM taxes and the Acute Care sale timing leave net debt open. Taxes on the gain are to be funded from the revolver and cash in an amount not stated, income taxes payable rose to USD 194.638 million from USD 18.787 million, and the sale for about USD 530 million may close only in 2027. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 54

The company is smaller and still being reshaped. Continuing operations are 60.44% of FY2025 combined net revenues, about three quarters of nine-month growth was acquired, and three restructuring plans with charges of USD 79 million to USD 96 million run to 2028, so scale, stranded cost and integration execution are unproven. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 127; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; calculation C01; calculation C13; calculation C15

cells.text: Teleflex Incorporated, a Delaware corporation incorporated in 1943, is the registrant, the borrower under the Credit Agreement and the issuer of the senior notes. It is not a subsidiary inside a group filing, so issuer and group are one entity. Continuing operations exclude the OEM business and the Acute Care and Interventional Urology businesses, which are presented as discontinued operations.
Common stock listed on the New York Stock Exchange as TFX; Commission file number 1-5353; large accelerated filer; principal executive offices at Wayne, Pennsylvania.

Medical devices, specifically single-use critical care and surgical devices; United States (Delaware corporation, Pennsylvania headquarters) with major manufacturing in the Czech Republic, Malaysia, Mexico and the United States. The run settings leave sector and country blank, so both are taken from the annual report.

"a global provider of medical technology products that enhance clinical benefits, improve patient and provider safety and reduce total procedural costs"; substantially all net revenues come from single-use medical devices used by hospitals and healthcare providers in high-acuity emergent procedures, and Teleflex states it is not dependent on any one end-market or procedure.
Three reportable segments from Q3 2026: Vascular, Interventional and Surgical, consistent with the reporting units; before that Americas, EMEA and Asia.

Vascular: Arrow catheters, EZ-IO intraosseous access and QuikClot hemostats. Interventional: coronary and peripheral catheters, GuideLiner, MANTA vascular closure and, since 2025-06-30, BIOTRONIK drug-coated balloons, stents and balloon catheters. Surgical: ligating clips, fascial closure systems, a powered bariatric stapler and surgical instruments.

rows.label: Products sold or held for sale

cells.text: OEM (custom extrusions, catheters, balloons, sutures and fibres for other device makers), sold on 2026-08-03; Acute Care (airway, pain management, respiratory, intra-aortic balloon pumps and urology care) and Interventional Urology (UroLift System and Barrigel), sale pending.

Hospitals and healthcare providers served through direct sales forces, independent representatives and distributors; outside the United States most customer relationships are with government entities. No customer, distributor or group purchasing concentration is stated, and the filings give no market share.

"The medical device industry is highly competitive"; Teleflex says it competes on clinical superiority, reliability, support and cost-effectiveness and that some competitors are larger with greater financial resources. No competitor is named.

Teleflex states it is not dependent on any single supplier for a substantial amount of materials or sterilization services; some vascular and surgical products are sterilised by a contract sterilizer that uses ethylene oxide and has faced legal proceedings at two plants.

About 15,500 employees at 2025-12-31 (3,700 in the United States and 11,800 in 38 other countries), of which 59% are in the global supply chain; about 110 properties including a leased 627,000 square foot distribution warehouse at Olive Branch, Mississippi.
Fourth-quarter sales are historically higher because of flu and disease patterns; most orders ship within days or weeks, so backlog is not a guide to future revenue.

Products are mainly Class I and Class II devices cleared through the FDA 510(k) process; the EU Medical Device Regulation certification is expected to be complete in 2026; the FDA quality system regulation was replaced by the QMSR on 2026-02-02.

Year ends 31 December; fiscal quarters were on a modified 5-4-4 calendar to 2025-12-31 and are calendar months from 2026-01-01. PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP has audited Teleflex since 1962 and gave an unqualified opinion dated 2026-02-27.

President and Chief Executive Officer since 2026-06-08; independent Chair since 2026-05-15 (the second Chair change of 2026); Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer since April 2025; two directors left on 2026-05-15 and three joined during 2026, one of them the new chief executive. Board composition, independence and committees are in a proxy statement that was not supplied.

Publicly held: 315 holders of record at 2026-02-24 and 39,661,261 shares outstanding at 2026-11-03; no controlling holder is named; beneficial ownership and any holding of the activist investor are not stated.

Quarterly dividend of USD 0.34 per share in each quarter of 2025 and 2026; share repurchase authorisation of USD 1.0 billion approved on 2025-12-09. The annual report and the first-quarter 2026 report said sale proceeds would be used "primarily to return capital to shareholders through share repurchases and pay down debt"; no leverage target is stated.

No private-equity sponsor, parent or controlling shareholder is identified; the run settings leave the sponsor blank. Governance risk therefore comes from a public board, an activist and management actions, not from sponsor behaviour.
No agency rating is stated in the supplied filings or the run settings.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Three transaction streams define the credit. In 2025 Teleflex bought the BIOTRONIK vascular intervention business, completed on 2025-06-30 for a net initial cash payment of EUR 704.3 million, or USD 825.2 million, against an agreed initial price of EUR 760 million before adjustments, funded with USD 700 million of delayed draw term loan borrowings and USD 140 million drawn on the revolver. On 2025-12-09 it signed agreements to sell the OEM business to Montagu and Kohlberg and the Acute Care and Interventional Urology businesses to Intersurgical for USD 2.0 billion in cash in total, about USD 1.5 billion and USD 530 million respectively. In 2026 it refinanced its bank debt and its 2027 notes and repaid bank debt from the OEM proceeds. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 124; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 8

The OEM sale closed on 2026-08-03 for net cash proceeds of USD 1.5 billion, USD 1.3 billion after tax, and a pre-tax gain of USD 1.0 billion; the June report had put the after-tax figure at approximately USD 1.2 billion and the later report controls. Ancillary agreements with the buyers run for up to 24 months and their results sit in selling, general and administrative expenses. Cash taxes on the gain are due in the fourth quarter of 2026 and will be funded with the revolver and cash. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 54

The Acute Care and Interventional Urology sale had not closed at the report date. Gross cash proceeds of approximately USD 530 million are expected, subject to working capital adjustments and transaction costs, closing may extend into 2027, and the transition agreements are to be executed at closing. The held-for-sale assets carry a valuation allowance of USD 758,859 thousand at 2026-09-30, which shows the agreed price is far below the carrying value of the businesses. The annual report and first-quarter report expected net after-tax proceeds of approximately USD 1.8 billion from both sales and said they would be used primarily to return capital to shareholders through share repurchases and pay down debt. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 30

On 2026-05-26 Teleflex replaced its 2022 credit agreement, which matured on 2027-11-04, with a new Credit Agreement: a five-year revolver of USD 1.0 billion and a Term A-1 loan of USD 500.0 million, both maturing on 2031-05-26, and a Term A-2 loan of USD 700.0 million maturing on 2028-05-26. It is guaranteed by substantially all material domestic subsidiaries, secured on substantially all assets of the company and each guarantor, and carries a maximum total net leverage ratio of 4.50 to 1.00 and a minimum interest coverage ratio of 3.00 to 1.00, against 3.50 to 1.00 at 2025-12-31; no reported ratio, headroom or letters of credit figure is stated for 2026-09-30. On 2026-06-15 Teleflex issued USD 500.0 million of senior notes due 2032, which with cash on hand redeemed the USD 500.0 million of senior notes due 2027 and raised the coupon on the replaced notes by 1.25 percentage points. In August 2026 it repaid the Term A-2 loan and USD 490.0 million of the revolver. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 137; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 139; calculation C12

Borrowings at 2026-09-30 were USD 60.0 million on the revolver, USD 496.875 million on Term A-1, USD 500.0 million of notes due 2028, USD 500.0 million of notes due 2032 and USD 75.0 million under the receivables securitization program: total principal of USD 1,631.875 million and a carrying value of USD 1,618.956 million, down by USD 1,018.125 million of principal since 2025-12-31. The notes due 2028 mature on 2028-06-01; the securitization maturity and the Term A-1 amortization are not stated. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 140; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 141; calculation C11

Shareholder returns run alongside debt repayment. The board authorised repurchases of up to USD 1.0 billion on 2025-12-09; Teleflex entered an accelerated repurchase agreement of USD 250 million with Truist Bank on 2026-08-07 that settled on 2026-10-07; and USD 600.0 million of stock was repurchased from 2026-01-01 to the report date, leaving USD 400.0 million of the authorisation. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 61; calculation C08

Earlier transactions explain what remains. Palette was bought in the fourth quarter of 2023 for an initial USD 594.9 million with up to USD 50 million of milestone payments and now sits in the sale perimeter, while a USD 46.7 million milestone claim stays with Teleflex; on 2025-02-27 Teleflex announced a plan to create a new independently traded company, which the sale agreements of 2025-12-09 replaced; and the Respiratory business was sold to Medline in 2021 and 2023. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2024-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net leverage fell to 2.82x on last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30 from 7.64x at year-end 2025, but the two ratios are not on one footing. At year-end 2025 consolidated debt, which also financed the businesses now held for sale, is set against the earnings of continuing operations alone. By 2026-09-30 the OEM sale proceeds had repaid the Term A-2 loan of USD 700.0 million and USD 490.0 million of the revolver. Holding EBITDA at the FY2025 level, net leverage at 2026-09-30 would still be 4.01x, so debt repayment explains most of the improvement and higher earnings the rest. The improvement for creditors rests mainly on sale proceeds applied to debt, not on a change in the earnings base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The earnings improvement is real but includes items that do not recur. Last-twelve-months EBITDA includes a patent settlement gain of USD 25.0 million and a tariff refund benefit of USD 25.3 million, about 11.95% of that EBITDA; without them net leverage would be 3.21x, an Analyst Judgement shown in the register and not used in any fixed row. FY2025 earnings, by contrast, carry a non-cash asset impairment and a currency hedge gain, but both sit in FY2025 and in the nine months of 2025, so they cancel out of the last-twelve-months figure. The strongest contrary evidence is the rise in reported gross margin to 59.8% in nine months 2026 from 57.1%, which the issuer attributes mainly to lower VI Business inventory step-up charges and to the tariff refunds; the step-up fade is durable but the refunds are not, and a fourth quarter without one-off gains would settle how much of the improvement lasts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover on cash interest is modest and cannot be updated. EBITDA covered cash interest paid 2.48x in FY2025 against 2.70x in FY2024, and accrued interest expense, which is lower because swap interest benefits reduce it, was covered 2.95x and 3.18x. On the same accrued basis last-twelve-months cover is 4.09x, which reflects both higher earnings and lower debt after the sale proceeds. Nine-month cash interest paid is not stated, so a 2026 cash cover cannot be built.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation improved but shareholder returns absorbed more than it. Last-twelve-months free cash flow after capital expenditure is positive and far above FY2025, which was close to zero after a build-up of receivables and higher tax payments, but it includes the patent settlement and tariff refunds in operating cash flow. In nine months 2026 cash paid for share repurchases was 3.08 times free cash flow, so the OEM sale proceeds also went to shareholders as well as to debt, and a further USD 41.4 million was repurchased after the quarter end. The remaining repurchase authorization means further payouts could slow deleveraging.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate against near-term debt but is not fully measured. Cash plus the undrawn revolver before letters of credit is large against the USD 87.5 million of borrowings due within 12 months, and the securitization program has USD 75.0 million drawn, the maximum stated at year-end 2025. Income taxes payable rose by USD 175.851 million over the nine months, and the issuer expects to fund cash taxes on the OEM gain from the revolver and cash in the fourth quarter, which will reduce liquidity and raise net debt by an amount the filing does not state. The nearest dated bullet maturity is the 2028 notes of USD 500.0 million, and the May 2026 refinancing moved the revolver and Term A-1 to 2031; the Acute Care and Interventional Urology sale, expected to bring about USD 530 million gross, would lower net debt if it closes, and closing may slip into 2027.

The OEM sale is a multi-figure event whose roles are kept apart: net cash proceeds of USD 1.5 billion, after-tax proceeds of USD 1.3 billion in the latest report, a pre-tax gain recognised in discontinued operations, and an investing inflow in the cash flow statement; the June 2026 report gave a lower after-tax figure and the later report controls.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and transaction review for Teleflex Inc (issuer tfx-96943), as of 2026-11-18, under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the business and operating model, ownership and control, group and debt structure, strategic transactions, governance record and capital-allocation behaviour in the 2024 and 2025 annual reports and the three 2026 quarterly reports. Leverage, liquidity and covenant headroom are left to other analyses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The run settings leave sector, country and sponsor blank; they are not issuer evidence and none is treated as zero. A retrieval record found beside the filings is not a source.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Teleflex is shrinking into a narrower vascular, interventional and surgical device group, and creditors now depend on new leadership splitting sale proceeds between bank debt repayment and share buybacks, the two uses management named.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The retained franchise is profitable: nine-month segment operating profit rose 20.0% and the bank facilities now run to 2031. Against that, 2026 growth was bought through the BIOTRONIK acquisition, the chief executive, Chair and board all changed during 2026, an activist wants strategic alternatives reviewed, and the Acute Care and Interventional Urology sale has slipped towards 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business creditors keep is smaller, and about three quarters of its 2026 revenue growth was bought rather than earned. Continuing operations were 60.44% of FY2025 combined net revenues, with the other 39.56% sold or held for sale. Net revenues rose 18.4% in the nine months of 2026, but USD 198.1 million of the USD 262.7 million increase, or 75.41%, came from the BIOTRONIK business bought on 2025-06-30, and third-quarter revenue rose only 0.2%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 124; 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 127; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation C01; calculation C04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interventional is the growth engine and the weak point. It supplied 37.17% of nine-month segment revenue after the acquisition, yet its segment margin was 10.37% against 14.10% a year earlier, its third-quarter revenue fell 2.6%, and its fair value exceeded carrying value by only about 15%, a cushion that a 1% rise in the discount rate would cut to below 5%. A further shortfall in the acquired business would first appear as an impairment signal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance changed on every front in 2026, and the filings do not yet state how the new board will weigh creditors against shareholders. The Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer left on 2026-01-08, an interim chief executive served for five months and a new one started on 2026-06-08; an independent Chair was appointed on 2026-01-08 and replaced on 2026-05-15; two directors left on 2026-05-15 and three joined, on 2026-05-15, 2026-06-08 and 2026-09-08; and an activist called for board changes and a review of strategic alternatives on 2026-03-27. No leverage target or credit rating is stated, and the proxy statement with board and ownership detail was not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management has said shareholders will share in the sale proceeds, and its 2026 actions are mixed rather than adverse. The 2025 annual report and the first-quarter 2026 report said the expected net after-tax proceeds of about USD 1.8 billion would be used "primarily to return capital to shareholders through share repurchases and pay down debt", and the later reports do not repeat the statement. After the OEM sale closed on 2026-08-03 the company repaid USD 1,190.0 million of bank debt, and from 2026-07-01 to the report date it also repurchased USD 350.0 million of stock, so repayment was 3.40 times repurchases in that window. Since 2026-01-01 repurchases total USD 600.0 million, USD 400.0 million of the USD 1.0 billion authorisation remains, and the dividend is USD 0.34 per share a quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Near-term risk sits in three dated items rather than in the franchise. The Acute Care and Interventional Urology sale, worth approximately USD 530 million gross, was first expected in the second half of 2026, then in the fourth quarter and now by the end of 2026 with closing possibly in 2027. Cash taxes on the OEM gain are due in the fourth quarter and will be funded from the revolver and cash, with income taxes payable of USD 194.6 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 18.8 million at 2025-12-31, so part of the August debt reduction is likely to be re-borrowed. Former Palette shareholders also sued on 2026-04-29 for milestone payments of USD 46.7 million against a contingent consideration liability of USD 47.3 million.

fields.value: Debt is issued at the parent and guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries, and the guarantor perimeter moved twice in 2026. Substantially all material domestic subsidiaries guarantee the bank facilities and both note series, and the bank facilities are secured on substantially all assets, while the security of the notes is not stated and the non-guarantor subsidiaries are not listed. Obligor group total assets at 2025-12-31 were USD 2,797.8 million in the annual report, USD 2,831.2 million after the first recast and USD 5,011.1 million after the second, so guarantor-level readings are not comparable across reports. The 2026 refinancing replaced the 2027 notes with 2032 notes at a coupon 1.25 percentage points higher and extended the revolver and Term A-1 to 2031.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall governance and sponsor risk is medium: no sponsor controls the company, reporting is regular and audited, and debt repayment so far exceeds buybacks, but shareholder returns, leadership turnover and unstated financial policy leave the use of the remaining proceeds open.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 104–109; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against caution is what management has done with cash. It repaid the USD 700.0 million Term A-2 loan and USD 490.0 million of the revolver within weeks of the OEM closing, extended the revolver and Term A-1 to 2031, redeemed the 2027 notes, and raised segment operating profit 20.0% in nine months with Vascular up 16.5% and Surgical up 34.3%. No acquisition, extraordinary dividend or creditor-adverse transaction is disclosed after 2025, repurchases to date are smaller than debt repayment, and the dividend is unchanged at USD 0.34 per share.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, pages 48–49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tfx.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would turn more cautious if the Acute Care and Interventional Urology proceeds, or the remaining USD 400.0 million authorisation and a larger one, went mainly to buybacks while the fourth-quarter taxes are drawn on the revolver; if the Palette claim succeeds above the contingent consideration liability; if the Acute Care sale slips beyond 2027 or fails; or if the review of strategic alternatives the activist wants ends in a sale of the company, which could engage the notes' repurchase right on a change of control if a ratings downgrade accompanies it. It would improve if the new chief executive states a leverage policy, if sale proceeds are applied to debt, and if the guarantor perimeter and segment reporting stop changing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three transaction streams define the credit. In 2025 Teleflex bought the BIOTRONIK vascular intervention business, completed on 2025-06-30 for a net initial cash payment of EUR 704.3 million, or USD 825.2 million, against an agreed initial price of EUR 760 million before adjustments, funded with USD 700 million of delayed draw term loan borrowings and USD 140 million drawn on the revolver. On 2025-12-09 it signed agreements to sell the OEM business to Montagu and Kohlberg and the Acute Care and Interventional Urology businesses to Intersurgical for USD 2.0 billion in cash in total, about USD 1.5 billion and USD 530 million respectively. In 2026 it refinanced its bank debt and its 2027 notes and repaid bank debt from the OEM proceeds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The OEM sale closed on 2026-08-03 for net cash proceeds of USD 1.5 billion, USD 1.3 billion after tax, and a pre-tax gain of USD 1.0 billion; the June report had put the after-tax figure at approximately USD 1.2 billion and the later report controls. Ancillary agreements with the buyers run for up to 24 months and their results sit in selling, general and administrative expenses. Cash taxes on the gain are due in the fourth quarter of 2026 and will be funded with the revolver and cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Acute Care and Interventional Urology sale had not closed at the report date. Gross cash proceeds of approximately USD 530 million are expected, subject to working capital adjustments and transaction costs, closing may extend into 2027, and the transition agreements are to be executed at closing. The held-for-sale assets carry a valuation allowance of USD 758,859 thousand at 2026-09-30, which shows the agreed price is far below the carrying value of the businesses. The annual report and first-quarter report expected net after-tax proceeds of approximately USD 1.8 billion from both sales and said they would be used primarily to return capital to shareholders through share repurchases and pay down debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On 2026-05-26 Teleflex replaced its 2022 credit agreement, which matured on 2027-11-04, with a new Credit Agreement: a five-year revolver of USD 1.0 billion and a Term A-1 loan of USD 500.0 million, both maturing on 2031-05-26, and a Term A-2 loan of USD 700.0 million maturing on 2028-05-26. It is guaranteed by substantially all material domestic subsidiaries, secured on substantially all assets of the company and each guarantor, and carries a maximum total net leverage ratio of 4.50 to 1.00 and a minimum interest coverage ratio of 3.00 to 1.00, against 3.50 to 1.00 at 2025-12-31; no reported ratio, headroom or letters of credit figure is stated for 2026-09-30. On 2026-06-15 Teleflex issued USD 500.0 million of senior notes due 2032, which with cash on hand redeemed the USD 500.0 million of senior notes due 2027 and raised the coupon on the replaced notes by 1.25 percentage points. In August 2026 it repaid the Term A-2 loan and USD 490.0 million of the revolver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 1 | Financial policy and use of the remaining proceeds | USD 600.0 million repurchased since 2026-01-01, USD 400.0 million of authorisation left, USD 1,190.0 million of bank debt repaid since 2026-08-03, no leverage target or rating, and a stated intent in the 2025 annual report and the first-quarter report to return capital and repay debt that later reports omit | Repurchases are discretionary and can be sized to cash on hand, so free cash flow and the pending sale proceeds may go to shareholders while the revolver funds taxes | Leverage of 2.82x at 2026-09-30 (2.92x after later repurchases, 1.56x if the Acute Care sale closes, OEM tax effect not established) is a result of the first proceeds, not a commitment | Negative | Medium |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 2 | Debt reduction and extended maturities | Principal fell by USD 1,018.125 million to USD 1,631.875 million; revolver and Term A-1 mature 2031-05-26; first note maturity USD 500.0 million on 2028-06-01; USD 87.5 million due within 12 months | Repayment removes the 2027 bullet and lowers interest cost, and no large maturity falls within 18 months | Lower probability of a liquidity or refinancing event over the next two years | Positive | High |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 3 | Cash taxes on the OEM gain | Taxes are expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 and funded from the revolver and cash; income taxes payable were USD 194.638 million against USD 18.787 million at year-end 2025; the amount is not stated | A revolver draw reverses part of the August repayment and cuts cash | Net debt rises by an unstated amount, so moderate leverage could weaken; no pro forma figure is established | Negative | Medium |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 4 | Interventional margin, volume and goodwill cushion | Margin 10.37% against 14.10%; third-quarter revenue down 2.6% on lower volume and price decreases; goodwill cushion about 15%, below 5% after a 1% rise in the discount rate; 32.77% of nine-month operating income | Rivalry and integration cost keep the acquired margin thin, and a shortfall would first appear as an impairment signal and then as lower earnings | Earnings and equity are exposed to one acquired segment, and unallocated costs leave little buffer behind segment profit | Negative | High |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 5 | Vascular and Surgical profitability with low capital intensity | Segment margins 38.12% and 45.10%; revenue up 7.2% and 8.4% without acquisitions; capital expenditure 3.47% of net revenues; last-twelve-months free cash flow USD 242.99 million, 57.71% of EBITDA | Volume and price growth on high-margin single-use products gives operating leverage and cash that does not depend on asset sales | Supports debt service and moderate deleveraging from operations | Positive | High |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 6 | One-off gains and temporary cash flow support | USD 25.0 million settlement gain and USD 25.3 million of tariff refunds are 11.95% of EBITDA; margin 16.44% without them; operating cash flow helped by lower tax payments and vendor timing | Receipts that do not repeat flatter EBITDA and free cash flow, so reported leverage understates the underlying ratio | Leverage on the earnings base without the gains is 3.21x, and a fourth quarter without refunds would show how much improvement lasts | Negative | High |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 7 | Liquidity and interest cover | Cash covers 86.09% of the 2028 notes; undrawn revolver up to USD 940 million before letters of credit; EBITDA covers run-rate coupon cost 5.04x, or 4.43x without the one-offs | Cash and committed facilities exceed the only large maturity 2.74 times and coupon cost is a fraction of EBITDA | Debt service capacity is sound while the revolver stays largely undrawn | Positive | Medium |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 8 | Covenant headroom and rating not established | Credit Agreement requires net leverage of at most 4.50x and interest coverage of at least 3.00x; no 2026 ratio, compliance statement, letters of credit figure or agency rating is reported | The tests use definitions the filings do not give, so cushion cannot be measured and market access cannot be anchored | The adequate view cannot be tested against the one hard constraint on leverage | Negative | Low |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 9 | Leadership change and activist pressure | Chief executive, Chair and three directors changed in 2026; an activist asked on 2026-03-27 for board changes and a review of strategic alternatives | New decision makers with no stated leverage tolerance could change use of proceeds or pursue a sale or recapitalisation | Policy risk is higher until the new team states a leverage policy | Negative | Medium |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 10 | Smaller, reshaped company | Continuing operations are 60.44% of FY2025 combined net revenues; three restructuring plans with charges of USD 79 million to USD 96 million and savings of USD 74 million to USD 86 million a year run to 2028 | Cash costs and stranded costs come before savings, and about three quarters of nine-month growth was acquired | Scale, cost removal and integration execution are unproven | Negative | Medium |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit analysis of Teleflex Inc (issuer tfx-96943), as of 2026-11-18, under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the continuing company after the 2026 sales: business risk, cash-flow durability, leverage, liquidity, refinancing and financial policy, drawn from the 2024 and 2025 annual reports, the three 2026 quarterly reports and the supplied Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance analyses. Legal and covenant basket analysis, recovery waterfalls, relative value and position sizing are outside this analysis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The run settings leave sector, country and sponsor blank; they are not issuer evidence and none is treated as zero. A retrieval record found beside the filings is not a source.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Teleflex is an adequate credit that has improved through asset sales more than through earnings, and creditors now depend on how management splits the proceeds still to come between debt and shareholders. Net leverage was 2.82x at 2026-09-30 against 7.64x at year-end 2025 on a narrower earnings base. It is 2.92x after USD 41.4 million of later repurchases and 1.56x if the Acute Care and Interventional Urology sale closes at about USD 530 million, while the effect of fourth-quarter taxes on the OEM gain is not established.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The retained business turned 57.71% of last-twelve-months EBITDA into free cash flow and has no note maturity before 2028-06-01, but USD 50.3 million of one-off gains sits in last-twelve-months EBITDA, shareholder payments were 2.53 times free cash flow, and covenant headroom is not reported.
